quotes.text: You can also create and manage payment links through [Checkout studio](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout-studio.md), which provides a centralized Dashboard hub for configuring and monitoring your Checkout integrations, including Payment Links.
By default, the maximum payment amount is 10,000.00 USD. Contact us using the form at [Stripe support](https://support.stripe.com) to increase this limit.
You can’t add any other line items and the quantity can only be `1`.
Some payment methods, such as bank debits or vouchers, might take between 2 and 14 days to confirm the payment.
Adaptive Pricing is always enabled for Payment Links.

old_evidence.text: By default, the maximum payment amount is 10,000.00 SGD. Contact us using the form at [Stripe support](https://support.stripe.com) to increase this limit.
You can include one line item for customer-defined prices.
You can add up to 20 line items for flat rate prices.

findings: The November capture adds Checkout studio as a Dashboard hub for creating and managing Payment Links (new raw:11 and See also:153). This is a new same-URL discovery route; the old capture lacks it. The linked Checkout studio page itself was not read here, so do not infer additional studio capabilities.

For customer-chosen-price links, the November API guidance says the sole line item must have quantity 1 (new raw:107). The April capture stated one line item (old raw:132) but did not expressly state quantity 1 in prose; its nearby curl example used quantity 1. Existing shared source line 47 and concept line 57 mention the one-line-item rule but omit the explicit quantity constraint. Recommend a narrow addition to the create-specific section, with this URL's November provenance.

The April Dashboard customer-chosen-price example states a default maximum of 10,000.00 SGD (old raw:33), while November states 10,000.00 USD (new raw:36), both with a support route to request an increase. Source line 55 and concept line 136 unqualifiedly say 10,000 SGD; revise them to record the two capture-specific wordings and avoid claiming a verified universal currency conversion, limit change, or merchant-specific applicability.

Several November API examples use curl rather than the old Node samples (new raw:54-93 versus old raw:51-112); parameter links and list numbering also changed. The variable-pricing example has a separate substantive example correction described below. Core 20 flat-rate line-item limit, subscription price and subscription_data trial example, variable pricing, mobile iOS restriction, dynamic payment methods, asynchronous fulfillment, and Adaptive Pricing remain in this same-URL capture (new raw:64,85,97-118,122-145).

The customer-chosen-price subsection has a more specific example repair than the overall sample-language shift: old raw:123-129 first creates a custom_unit_amount Price, but old raw:134-141 then inlines fixed price_data with unit_amount=1000 in the Payment Link curl example. New raw:99-105 creates the custom Price and new raw:107,109-113 passes its PRICE_ID in the sole line_item with quantity 1. Recommend documenting that corrected variable-pricing sequence and not presenting the old fixed-unit_amount inline example as valid customer-chosen-price guidance. This capture difference does not prove a new universal API restriction; ordinary fixed-product price_data inline creation remains separately documented at new raw:73-83.

The mapped source is a multi-raw Payment Links summary with eight April raw_files at source lines 7-14 and distinct raw-source descriptions at lines 65-72. Add the November create capture only for create-specific evidence, preserving all unrelated overview/share/track/buy-button/customize/shipping/promotions dated histories and their claims.

unresolved_questions: The captures alone do not establish why the displayed currency changed or which amount and currency apply to any particular merchant, account, locale, or current Dashboard session.
The Checkout studio target page was not part of this job, so its detailed features and limitations remain unverified here.
